newsitem.title: USA: PG&E says Diablo Canyon nuke refuel starts Apr 19.
newsitem.headline: PG&E says Diablo Canyon nuke refuel starts Apr 19.

text.p: PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas & Electric Co will shut its 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 1 in central California April 19 for a 36-day refueling outage, a company spokesman said Wednesday.
PG&E said several months ago the outage would start about May 3.
Diablo Canyon's 1,073 MW unit 2 is next scheduled to shut for refueling on September 20.
Elsewhere in the region, the 1,080 MW unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in southern California is scheduled to shut for 65 days of refueling and maintenance on April 12.
San Onofre's 1,070 MW unit 2 has been down for refueling and repairs since November 30 and is due to begin ramping up to full power on Thursday.
The 1,221 MW unit 3 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant in Arizona was shut February 22 for refueling which is due to conclude April 3.
Palo Verde's 1,221 MW unit 2 is scheduled to shut for regular refueling on September 20.
The 1,158 WNP-2 nuclear unit in Washington state is currently operating at 100 percent during peak demand morning hours and at 70 percent during other hours.
The unit is scheduled to shut for refueling April 18, but is tentatively scheduled to go off-line nextg week due to the regional abundance of lower-cost hydropower.
